items.title: Pre-flight prints the same guider problem twice and both times tells you to connect PHD2, in a build that ships its own native guider
items.summary: Two halves, one already closed and one still live. The DUPLICATION was fixed by an earlier wave: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/rules/equipment_rules.dart:105-148 now emits per-node 'Guider Not Connected' warnings and keeps the generic 'No Guider Connected' summary as a fallback ONLY when no enabled node can be attributed, with a regression test already in place. The BACKEND-AWARENESS half was still real and is now fixed. The old text said '<node> requires a guider (PHD2)' and, unconditionally, 'Connect to PHD2 in the Guiding panel.' I confirmed against the Guiding panel that this is bad advice, not just imprecise: desktop_sections.dart:230 only renders a Connect button when `isPhd2Guider` is true, and for any other backend it renders an 'Equipment' button (desktop_sections.dart:252) that navigates away. This build discovers and connects a 'Built-in Multi-Star Guider' (native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/api/discovery.rs:779), so an operator running the native guider was sent to a panel with no Connect button on it. The rule now drops PHD2 from the description and routes the hint through a new `_guiderResolutionHint(GuiderState)`: PHD2 selected -> 'Connect to PHD2 in the Guiding panel.'; another backend selected -> 'Connect <device name> in the Equipment panel.'; nothing selected -> 'Connect a guider in the Equipment panel - the built-in multi-star guider, or PHD2.' The hint is computed once and shared by both the per-node warnings and the fallback summary, so the two cannot drift.
items.test: packages/skotiq_core/test/providers/sequence/sequence_validation_ref_aware_test.dart :: 'missing-guider advice names the panel that can connect the selected backend' - drives the rule with the built-in guider selected, PHD2 selected, and nothing selected, and asserts each hint names the panel that can actually connect that guider. 25/25 tests in the file pass.
items.revert_check: Independently re-run. Reverted packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/rules/equipment_rules.dart:116 from `final hint = _guiderResolutionHint(gs);` back to `const hint = 'Connect to PHD2 in the Guiding panel.';` -> 'missing-guider advice names the panel that can connect the selected backend' FAILS with `Expected: not contains 'PHD2' / Actual: 'Connect to PHD2 in the Guiding panel.'`. Restored -> 25/25 pass. Also re-confirmed the fix is not INVERTED by reading the panel it now points away from: guiding_screen_parts/desktop_sections.dart renders a Connect button only in the `!isConnected && isPhd2Guider` branch and otherwise renders an 'Equipment' button that does `context.go('/equipment')`, so 'Connect a guider in the Equipment panel' is where a non-PHD2 backend genuinely has to be connected.

items.title: Node palette search ranks Smart Exposure above the node literally named 'Dither' when you search 'Dither'
items.summary: The location named in the finding is already correct - packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/sequencer/widgets/node_palette.dart:54 and .../sequencer_screen_parts/node_palette.dart:35 both route through the shared `rankNodePaletteMatches` (node_palette_search.dart), which scores exact name 100 / prefix 80 / name-substring 60 / description 20 and hoists the best-scoring category, with tests in sequencer_jank_p3_test.dart. But a THIRD node-palette search box was still running the old, unranked filter: the Insert Above / Insert Below picker reached from the tree's right-click menu (`_InsertNodePicker` in sequence_tree_context_menu.dart) filtered on `name.contains(q) || description.contains(q)` and rendered survivors in catalogue order, so typing 'Dither' there still put Smart Exposure first - the exact failure the finding describes, on the surface a user reaches when they right-click to insert a node at a specific slot. Moved it onto the shared ranker.
items.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/sequencer/sequence_tree_context_menu_test.dart :: 'Insert picker ranks an exact name match above a description match' - overrides nodePaletteProvider with a Smart Exposure item whose description contains 'dither' plus a node named 'Dither', opens the picker, types 'dither', and asserts the rendered y of the Dither row is above the Smart Exposure row.
items.revert_check: Independently re-run. Restored the old `name || description` catalogue-order filter in place of packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/sequencer/widgets/sequence_tree_context_menu.dart:650 (`final filtered = rankNodePaletteMatches(categories, _query);`) -> 'Insert picker ranks an exact name match above a description match' FAILS. Restored -> 13/13 tests in the file pass. Also re-confirmed the ranker is the ONLY search path left in the sequencer: `grep rankNodePaletteMatches` returns exactly three non-test call sites (widgets/node_palette.dart:60, sequencer_screen_parts/node_palette.dart:35, sequence_tree_context_menu.dart:650) and no `item.description.toLowerCase().contains` survives in any palette.

items.title: Continue Session reports '0 minutes integration' for a session that has 12s of integration on the card behind it
items.summary: Real, and the finding's `screen:sequencer/session_handoff_dialog.dart` unit is the wrong file - the Progress row is built by packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/quick_start_dialog.dart:324-340 (the 'Continue Session' dialog) and formatted by `_formatIntegration(double hours)` at :134, which returned `'${hours.toStringAsFixed(1)} hours'` above 1h and `'${(hours*60).round()} minutes'` below it. 12s = 0.0033h rounds to 0, so a run with four real light frames on disk announced '0 minutes integration'. Fixed at the cause by giving the app ONE integration formatter: new `formatIntegrationSeconds` / `formatIntegrationHours` in packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/utils/duration_format.dart (h/m/s, rounding to whole seconds first so 59.6s reads '1m 0s' not '60s', and clamping negative/non-finite to '0s'). `ParsedRunStats.formatDuration` - the formatter the dashboard's last-night recap card, the history tab and the post-session dialog already render - now delegates to it, and the Continue Session dialog calls it too, so the two surfaces cannot disagree about the same run. 12s now reads '12s' in both places.
items.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/widgets/quick_start_dialog_integration_format_test.dart - 4 tests: the 12s run renders '4/4 frames captured, 12s integration' and no '0 minutes' anywhere; 90s renders '1m 30s' not '2 minutes'; 1.2h renders '1h 12m 0s'; and a unit check that ParsedRunStats.formatDuration(12) == formatIntegrationHours(12/3600) == '12s'.
items.revert_check: Independently re-run. Reverted packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/quick_start_dialog.dart:138 (`String _formatIntegration(double hours) => formatIntegrationHours(hours);`) to the old whole-minutes body -> 3 of the 4 tests FAIL. Restored -> 4/4 pass. Also checked the shared-formatter change does not RELOCATE the problem onto the surfaces that were already correct: the old `ParsedRunStats.formatDuration` body and `formatIntegrationSeconds` agree on every well-formed input (12s -> '12s' both ways); they diverge only where the old one was wrong (59.6s was '60s', now '1m 0s'; 3599.6s was '59m 60s', now '1h 0m 0s'; a negative value floored to '-1h ...', now '0s'). `stats.formatDuration` has exactly two render call sites - last_night_recap_card.dart:104/:124 and history_tab.dart:570 - and no test anywhere else asserts the old shape.

items.title: A node can only be reordered by drag; the node context menu offers just Duplicate and Delete
items.summary: The finding's inventory of the menu is stale - the right-click menu already carried eight entries (Skip to here, Insert Above, Insert Below, Duplicate, Group into Sequential, Group into Parallel, Disable/Enable, Delete), and Move Up / Move Down already existed in the row's kebab 'More Actions' menu (node_item.dart:937-962), so drag was NOT the only route. What was real: the right-click menu itself had no reorder, which is the menu an operator opens when they want to move a node; and the in-code justification for that split cited a 'Shift+Up / Shift+Down keyboard shortcut wired in sequence_tree_shortcuts.dart' that does not reorder anything - kSequenceTreeShortcuts:68-71 binds Shift+Arrow to EXTEND THE SELECTION. Added Move Up / Move Down to SequenceTreeContextMenu, going through the same `moveNode(id, parentId, index)` call the kebab and drag-drop use (one undo entry shape, one reindex path), disabled with an explanatory tooltip on the root and at either end of a sibling list. Corrected the false comment in node_item.dart rather than leaving a note that misdescribes the keymap.
items.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/sequencer/sequence_tree_context_menu_test.dart - 3 tests: 'Move Up shifts the node one slot earlier among its siblings' and 'Move Down shifts the node one slot later among its siblings' assert the parent's childIds order after picking the entry; 'Move Up is disabled on the first sibling and changes nothing' asserts the disabled entry is a no-op.
items.revert_check: Independently re-run. Removed the two `entry(_TreeMenuAction.moveUp/moveDown, ...)` blocks at packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/sequencer/widgets/sequence_tree_context_menu.dart:244-256 -> all 3 tests FAIL ('Move Up shifts...', 'Move Down shifts...', 'Move Up is disabled on the first sibling'). Restored -> 13/13 tests in the file pass. Separately: the finding's report that a 9-step drag left the order unchanged is NOT evidence of a broken drop handler - node_tree_view.dart:397 wraps the row in a `LongPressDraggable` with `delay: Duration(milliseconds: 150)`, so a synthetic press that starts moving immediately never arms the drag. Left as-is; the menu route is what the finding actually asked for.

items.title: There is no keyboard shortcut that reorders a node (the finding proposed Alt+Arrow)
items.summary: Split out of the reorder finding because it is a keymap decision, not a defect. Reorder is now reachable by mouse from two menus and is keyboard-REACHABLE transitively (tab to the row's kebab, Enter, arrow to Move Up), but there is no direct binding: sequence_tree_shortcuts.dart binds bare Arrow to move the selection, Shift+Arrow to extend it, Left/Right to collapse/expand and Enter to jump to the properties panel.
items.options: (a) Bind Alt+Up / Alt+Down to reorder the selected node - the editor convention (VS Code, most tree editors), free of any binding currently in kSequenceTreeShortcuts or the top-level sequencer_screen.dart map, and it makes the fastest path for a 30-instruction sequence a keyboard one. (b) Leave it: the tree's keymap is deliberately small and obvious (the file says so in its own header), Alt is the menu-mnemonic modifier on Windows/Linux and can collide with window-manager bindings, and NINA/SGP ship no such binding either, so nobody arrives expecting it.
items.recommendation: (a). Reordering is the one structural edit an operator repeats dozens of times while building a sequence, and it is the only one with no direct key. But this changes the app's keyboard contract - it belongs in the shortcut help sheet and the docs - so it is the owner's call, not mine.
